strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with vectorized local ops
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce calls (one per stage) with fully vectorized scale/unscale operations between stages using tensor slicing and broadcasting. 8 all-reduce dispatches total. Trades dispatch count for simplicity and matches the reference structure with minimal optimization.

strategies.name: Fused local-op batching between all-reduces
strategies.desc: Pre-computes scale factors as tensors and uses in-place operations to eliminate intermediate clones where safe, applying multiple scale/unscale transformations in single kernel launches. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but reduces local compute overhead by batching element-wise operations and eliminating redundant memory allocations.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter then all-gather pipeline
strategies.desc: Decomposes each all-reduce into reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing computation of scale/unscale operations during the all-gather phase to overlap communication with computation. 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but exploits pipelining opportunities to hide local operation latency.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction with node-local aggregation
strategies.desc: Exploits multi-node topology by performing intra-node reductions first, applying transformations on aggregated node-level results, then inter-node reductions. Reduces cross-node bandwidth requirements at the cost of additional collective calls (potentially 16-24 dispatches depending on whether intra-node uses separate collectives).

strategies.name: Bucketed parallel all-reduce with rank-sharded computation
strategies.desc:
Partitions the 224-rank world into groups and performs all-reduce on subsets concurrently where dependencies permit, applying scale transformations only to relevant shard ranges per rank. Uses approximately 8 all-reduce dispatches but with smaller participation sets and localized computation patterns that may improve cache efficiency.
